subject: Order Form SLA: uptime & response time amendments
messages:
From: Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@halcyon.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@halcyon.ai, ops@halcyon.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Halcyon — proposed SLA redlines (order form)

Evelyn / Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The procurement team reviewed the draft order form and attached SLA and returned a redlined doc (attached). High level asks from Halcyon:

- Tighten P1 initial response to 15 minutes (we need faster on-call escalation)
- Exclude scheduled regional maintenance only if notified 72 hours in advance (they want more notice)
- Service credit cap: reduce from 25% of monthly fees to 15% — they prefer a lower cap
- Clarify measurement window: they propose a 30-day rolling availability SLO measured per-region

Can we confirm what we can accept vs where we need legal to push back? I can arrange a quick call if helpful.

Attached: Halcyon_SLA_Redline_v3.docx

—Thomas
Director of Ops, Halcyon AI

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@halcyon.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Halcyon — proposed SLA redlines (order form)

Thomas —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redline. Quick notes after a first pass:

- P1 initial response: 15m is aggressive for a hosted multi-tenant plan. We can commit to 15m for Dedicated customers and 30m for Hosted. If Halcyon is moving to Dedicated, we can mark 15m as "Dedicated-only".
- Scheduled maintenance notice: 72h notice is reasonable for planned maintenance; our standard is 48h. We can accept 72h for regionally scoped maintenance if they accept a slightly wider maintenance window (we'll propose a 4-hour window vs current 2-hour).
- Service credit cap: 15% is acceptable only if the uptime tiers are tightened (e.g., 99.95% baseline rather than 99.9%) — legal will push for the larger cap if we lower SLOs.
- Measurement window: 30-day rolling per-region is ok, but we need to include an escape for force majeure and emergency failovers (can't penalize for customer-triggered multi-region failover).

I'll loop in Legal to create a compromise redline that preserves our runway while addressing their ops concerns. Marissa / Karthik — can you review the attached support_matrix.csv for response ladders and confirm Dedicated vs Hosted wording?

Next step: I propose a 30-min call Wednesday to walk Halcyon through the changes and land on final redlines. Thomas — what times work?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@halcyon.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 10 Dec 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Halcyon — proposed SLA redlines (order form)

Evelyn / Thomas —

I reviewed Halcyon's redlines and drafted language for a middle ground. Key legal positions:

1) Initial response times:
   - Accept 15 minutes for P1 only when customer has Reserved/Dedicated capacity with 24x7 priority support add-on.
   - For Hosted customers, retain 30-minute P1 initial response.

2) Scheduled maintenance:
   - Accept 72-hour notification if maintenance is regional and non-disruptive to cross-region failover.
   - For global rolling updates that may impact failover, maintain 72-hour notice but include a clause that allows for emergency security hotfixes with 24-hour notice.

3) Service credit cap & calculation:
   - Propose a blended cap: 15% cap for the order form month 1–3 (introductory), reverting to 25% thereafter, or alternative: 15% cap if customer elects a reduced SLO (99.9%), 25% if customer keeps default SLO (99.95%).
   - Credits calculated as % of monthly recurring fees tied to affected region(s).

4) Measurement window:
   - 30-day rolling per-region OK; include explicit exclusions for force majeure, customer-initiated failovers, and scheduled maintenance windows.

I've updated Halcyon_SLA_Redline_v3.docx with these options and included bracketed choices to speed negotiations. Evelyn — please confirm which option you want us to present (blended cap vs tiered cap). Also attaching a proposed support_matrix.csv with response tiers and escalation SLAs.

-Lauren
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@halcyon.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Halcyon — proposed SLA redlines (order form)

Team —

Technical suggestion from ops side to reduce customer friction:

- If we accept 72h notice we should offer a defined maintenance cadence per region (e.g., monthly Saturday maintenance window between 0200–0600 local). This reduces surprise and helps Halcyon schedule cutovers.
- For P1 triage: propose an automated alert flow that creates a ticket in their PagerDuty with a Redwood runbook link. That will materially cut mean time to acknowledge.

I've attached deployment_schedule.xlsx with proposed maintenance cadence by region. If Halcyon signs Dedicated we can offer a 15m P1 SLA and a priority on-call roster. For Hosted, we maintain the 30m P1 and offer the priority add-on.

-Karthik
Head of Reliability Engineering

From: Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@halcyon.ai>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, procurement@halcyon.ai, ops@halcyon.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Halcyon — proposed SLA redlines (order form)

Evelyn / Lauren / Karthik —

Thanks — that read is helpful and the bracketed language gives us options. Halcyon prefers the tiered-cap approach: 15% cap if we accept a 99.9% SLO, otherwise 25% at 99.95%. We are inclined toward 99.95% but want the 15m P1 for all plans if possible — the Dedicated path is something we're evaluating but not committed to.

Two negotiation points from our side:

- Can you make the maintenance cadence an explicit calendar commitment (e.g., monthly scheduled window for region X) — we need a predictable calendar to coordinate customer cutovers.
- For initial response time, would Redwood consider a pilot: 3-month trial of 15m P1 on Hosted with an operational runbook (automated PD + runbook) and then revert if it impacts cost or reliability?

If you can accept a 3-month trial and calendarized maintenance windows, procurement is prepared to sign the order form with the tiered-cap language. We'll need DocuSign route once legal finalizes the bracketed picks.

—Thomas

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: Thomas Nguyen <t.nguyen@halcyon.ai>, procurement@halcyon.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Halcyon — proposed SLA redlines (order form)

Thomas —

Great — we can proceed on the tiered-cap approach and we accept the 3-month Hosted pilot for 15m P1 with the following guardrails:

- Pilot limited to Halcyon production workload with pre-approved contact routing (PagerDuty integration + a named Halcyon on-call list).
- During the pilot, Redwood will run a weekly ops sync and provide a short runbook. If the pilot causes measurable reliability regressions or cost delta >10% month-over-month attributable to the 15m SLA, Redwood may revert to 30m with 30 days' notice.
- Maintenance cadence: Redwood will publish a regional maintenance calendar (monthly Saturday window 02:00–06:00 local) and notify Halcyon 72 hours ahead. Emergency security hotfixes remain exempt with 24-hour notice.
- Final edits: Lauren will finalize bracketed language in Halcyon_SLA_Redline_v3.docx and route via DocuSign (link below).

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/EnvelopeSigning/ABCDEFG12345
Drive folder with final redlines: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdSLA-redlines

If that works, procurement — please confirm and we'll send the final order form this afternoon.

Thanks,
Evelyn
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
